cohort_total_n_excerpt: a case-control study was conducted in Hangzhou, China, with 130 prostate cancer patients and 274 hospital controls.
reason: The study evaluates overall prostate cancer risk in cases and hospital controls; no aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal incident endpoint is analyzed.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Intakes of vegetables and fruits rich in lycopene were also inversely associated with prostate cancer risk (odds ratio 0.18, 95% CI 0.08-0.39).
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported OR concerns overall prostate cancer risk, without an aggressive-disease restriction.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The protective effect of green tea was significant (odds ratio 0.14, 95% CI: 0.06-0.35) for the highest quartile relative to the lowest after adjusting for total vegetables and fruits intakes and other potential confounding factors.
estimate_classifications.reason: The green-tea estimate concerns overall prostate cancer risk.
